subject: RFP: Control plane segregation, telemetry exfil mitigations & artifact provenance — evidence packet
messages:
From: Alex Stone <alex.stone@everest.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@everest.com>
Date: 2026-09-26T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: Evidence request — control plane separation & telemetry exfil mitigations

Ben —

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of Everest Financial's security review for our procurement packet, we need an evidence bundle that describes how Redwood separates the control plane from customer inference/data paths, what telemetry is collected and how exfil is prevented, and how model/artifact provenance is asserted (hashing/signing). Specific asks:

- A network/zone diagram that shows control plane, data plane, and any bastions/edge proxies.
- A short threat-summary (3–5 bullets) describing the highest-priority attack paths for telemetry + mitigations.
- Artifact provenance workflow and the checksums/signing process for model artifacts.
- Retention/forwarding rules for telemetry and whether PII can appear in logs.

If you can provide a PDF/PNG diagram, a brief one-page threat summary, and a CSV of artifact checksums, I can attach them to the RFP. We have a tight timeline (need packet by Oct 1).

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Stone
Head of Infrastructure Risk, Everest Financial
security@everest.com

---
Note: please include internal contacts only from your sales/security leadership who will be listed on the packet.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP: Evidence request — control plane separation & telemetry exfil mitigations

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are three artifacts: a diagram (control-plane-separation-diagram.png), our telemetry policy PDF (telemetry-retention-and-filtering.pdf), and a CSV with artifact hash checksums (artifact-hash-checksums.csv). Short summary below and an inline diagram sketch to make the separation explicit.

Quick summary (high level):
- Control plane exclusively runs in a logically separated management VPC with mutual TLS to worker hosts. No customer inference traffic traverses the control plane VPC.
- Data plane (inference runtime) runs in customer-dedicated compute pools (hosted or private) with strictly scoped egress and sidecar proxies that enforce allowlists.
- Telemetry collection is agented at the host and sidecar, scrubbed by filtering rules before export, and forwarded to a telemetry pipeline over an authenticated channel with strict retention & role-based access.
- Model artifacts are stored in an immutable artifact store; each artifact is content-hash addressed and signed with HSM-backed keys. We provide a checksum CSV and the verification steps in the packet.

Inline ASCII diagram (simplified):

  +----------------------+      +----------------------+      +----------------------+
  |  Control Plane VPC   | <--> |  Management Bastion   | <--> |  Admin Workstations  |
  |  (metdata, control)  |      |  (jump / ops)         |      |  (RBAC enforced)     |
  +---------+------------+      +----------+-----------+      +----------+-----------+
            |                                ^                             |
            |                                |                             |
            v                                |                             v
  +----------------------+      +-------------+-----------+      +----------------------+
  | Artifact Store (S3)  |----->|  Artifact Verification   |<-----|  CI/CD (signing)      |
  |  (signed, immutable) |      |  (HSM signature check)  |      |  (HSM sign step)      |
  +----------------------+      +-------------------------+      +----------------------+

  (Data plane runtime clusters are in separate VPCs/subnets; network ACLs and sidecars enforce egress allowlists)

Telemetry flow (high level): host -> local sidecar agent (filter & redact) -> metrics/trace relay -> telemetry pipeline (ingest tier in private VPC) -> long-term store (restricted RBAC)

Attachments included: see file names above. For the artifact CSV, we include sha256 checksums and the signing key id. For any PII-related logs, our filters remove keys that match credit-card and SSN patterns; we also provide a sampling policy if customers opt in for debug traces.

Priya & Marissa — tagging you for the threat bullets and any additional evidence notes you want in the packet.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFP: Evidence request — control plane separation & telemetry exfil mitigations

Alex / Ben —

Adding the threat-summary and a short mitigation table per your ask. Quoting Ben below for context.

Top 4 threat scenarios (brief):
1) Telemetry exfil via compromised sidecar/process: mitigations — local filtering, export allowlists, mTLS to telemetry relay, and anomaly detection on outbound patterns.
2) Unauthorized control-plane access leading to model tampering: mitigations — control plane in dedicated VPC, strict IAM with customer-scoped roles, MFA + device posture for admin hosts, and HSM for signing artifacts.
3) Supply-chain artifact swap (attacker replaces model binary): mitigations — artifact immutability, content-addressable storage, signed releases, reproducible-build checks, and verification during deployment.
4) Cross-tenant data leakage in shared infra: mitigations — tenant network fencing, kernel namespacing and cgroup isolation, per-tenant runtime pools for high-sensitivity customers, and network microsegmentation.

Mitigation table (short):
- Detection: egress anomaly alerts, telemetry pipeline alerting (SLOs for bytes/requests).
- Prevention: strict egress allowlists, content sniffing & redactors, and signed artifacts enforced at deploy time.
- Recovery: immutable artifact snapshots & rollbacks, key-rotation playbooks, logged KMS/HSM actions for audit.

Evidence notes:
- The attached telemetry PDF lists filtering rules used in the sidecar and sample redaction regexes.
- The CSV contains sha256 checksums + signature key id for the model bundle referenced in your RFP (bundle v3.2).
- All control-plane admin actions are logged; logs are write-once for 90 days in a WORM store for forensics.

If you want, we can also provide a short recorded walkthrough (10–12 minutes) that shows the artifact verification step in CI — I can link it into the packet.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
